title: Peer/groupUpdate avatar object with fetchUrl
description:
Oracle: jmap-chat-spec 6bcd9d8 (quoted text). Mapped by wf_6712c4f8-c2b.

[chat-ext] Peer/groupUpdate avatarBlobId replaced by avatar object with fetchUrl
Spec (ff6b3b9): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md L667-668: "`avatar` (Object\|null, optional): : The group avatar image. MAY be present for `"create"` or `"updateMetadata"` actions. An Object carries the `contentType`, `size`, and `sha256` fields of an Attachment ({{JMAP-CHAT}}) plus `fetchUrl` (String) ... For `"updateMetadata"`, `null` removes the group avatar; absent leaves it unchanged."; L676: "After the authorization and `closedAt` checks above succeed, and only then, if `avatar` is an Object, the receiving server validates `contentType` and `size` ..., fetches the blob from `fetchUrl` with a signed request ... The avatar is best-effort ... A failed avatar never causes the request to be rejected"; L678: "it stores the fetched blob and sets the Chat's `avatarBlobId` to the local blobId; when `avatar` is `null`, it removes `avatarBlobId`."
Code: crate-jmap-chat-federation-types/src/peer.rs:552,653-655,680 PeerGroupUpdateArgs.avatar_blob_id; crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/group_update.rs:24,37,43-45 (docs); crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/group_update.rs:100 (create stores remote blob id as-is); crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/group_update.rs:147-150 (updateMetadata patches avatarBlobId; cannot express null removal); crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/outbound.rs:202,270-274 set_metadata sends local avatarBlobId; crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/deliver.rs:124-139 (fetch hook takes PeerAttachment only)
Now: The code sends and receives `avatarBlobId` (a sender-local blob id) and stores it verbatim on the receiver's Chat. A conformant peer's `avatar` object lands in `extra` and is ignored, so no avatar is ever fetched. `avatar: null` cannot remove an avatar.
Change: Replace avatar_blob_id with `avatar: Option<Option<PeerAvatar>>` carrying contentType/size/sha256/fetchUrl, so absent, null, and Object stay distinct. Inbound: after the auth and closedAt checks, validate contentType and size, fetch through a backend hook (generalise fetch_attachment or add fetch_avatar), and verify size and sha256. On any failure, apply the rest of the request and leave the avatar absent or current; never reject. On success set avatarBlobId to the local blob; null removes it. Outbound: build the avatar object from the local blob through a hook that mints the fetchUrl and records the grant before sending.
